edges.source: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy at Interval Cytoreductive Surgery
Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy at Interval Cytoreductive Surgery

edges.description: Intraperitoneal tumour cells establish peritoneal disease with ascites, and hyperthermic cisplatin is applied to that compartment as the perturbation. The model manipulates peritoneal dissemination under hyperthermic chemotherapy; it does not claim to reproduce the human transcoelomic mechanism itself.
edges.limitations: Heat is applied externally across the abdominal wall rather than by intraperitoneal perfusion at laparotomy, so the thermal and drug gradients across peritoneal deposits are not the clinical ones; murine peritoneal scale, syngeneic ID8/IE9 tumour biology and the absence of prior neoadjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel and cytoreduction all diverge from the OVHIPEC-1 setting. The source is a non-peer-reviewed preprint, so these results should not be transferred to human disease without corroboration.

nodes.description: BRCA1/2-deficient metastatic ovarian cancers exhibit homologous recombination deficiency, increased platinum sensitivity, and marked susceptibility to PARP inhibition, although acquired resistance eventually emerges in many cases.

evidence.reference_title: Comparison of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) as maintenance therapy for newly-diagnosed and platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer with BRCA mutational status: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: All PARPis showed significant benefit, with olaparib showing greater benefit in newly diagnosed and PSR OC women.

nodes.description: A humanised anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody added to carboplatin-paclitaxel and continued as maintenance. Two phase 3 trials established a modest but reproducible progression-free survival benefit: GOG-0218 (median PFS 14.1 vs 10.3 months with bevacizumab throughout) and ICON7 (restricted-mean PFS at 42 months 24.1 vs 22.4 months). Neither trial showed a significant overall survival benefit in the whole population; in ICON7 the benefit was larger in the subgroup at high risk of progression. Hypertension is the characteristic toxicity.

evidence.reference_title: Incorporation of bevacizumab in the primary treatment of ovarian cancer.
evidence.snippet: The median progression-free survival was 10.3 months in the control group, 11.2 in the bevacizumab-initiation group, and 14.1 in the bevacizumab-throughout group.

evidence.reference_title: Incorporation of bevacizumab in the primary treatment of ovarian cancer.
evidence.snippet: At the time of analysis, 76.3% of patients were alive, with no significant differences in overall survival among the three groups.

evidence.reference_title: A phase 3 trial of bevacizumab in ovarian cancer.
evidence.snippet: progression-free survival (restricted mean) at 42 months was 22.4 months without bevacizumab versus 24.1 months with bevacizumab

nodes.description: The first-line standard of care for advanced ovarian cancer, and the backbone that every other treatment in this entry is added to: maximal cytoreductive surgery aiming for no gross residual disease, combined with platinum-taxane chemotherapy. It is delivered either as primary debulking surgery followed by chemotherapy, or as neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery when tumour load or performance status makes upfront complete cytoreduction unlikely. The HIPEC entry below is an adjunct administered at that interval surgery, and the bevacizumab and PARP-inhibitor entries are added to this same chemotherapy backbone.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Pathway of Advanced Ovarian Cancer with Peritoneal Metastases
evidence.snippet: In this scenario, standard treatment includes a combination of cytoreductive surgery and carboplatinum–paclitaxel-based chemotherapy.

nodes.description: Heated cisplatin perfused through the peritoneal cavity at the time of interval cytoreductive surgery, after neoadjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel. The rationale is compartmental: metastatic ovarian cancer sits on peritoneal surfaces that intravenous drug reaches poorly, so the drug is delivered into the compartment that carries the tumour burden. In the OVHIPEC-1 phase 3 trial the addition of HIPEC extended median overall survival from 33.9 to 45.7 months without increasing grade 3-4 toxicity. Benefit appears specific to the interval (post-neoadjuvant) setting; it has not been shown after primary debulking surgery, and the mechanism of benefit is not established.
nodes.id: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy at Interval Cytoreductive Surgery

evidence.reference_title: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy in Ovarian Cancer.
evidence.snippet: the addition of HIPEC to interval cytoreductive surgery resulted in longer recurrence-free survival and overall survival than surgery alone and did not result in higher rates of side effects

evidence.reference_title: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy in Ovarian Cancer.
evidence.snippet: The median overall survival was 33.9 months in the surgery group and 45.7 months in the surgery-plus-HIPEC group.

evidence.reference_title: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy in the Management of Primary Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: A Debated Issue for Gynecologic Oncologists.
evidence.snippet: the available data from two phase III trials seem to suggest that the addition of HIPEC to interval debulking surgery after neoadjuvant chemotherapy significantly improves PFS and OS. Conversely, HIPEC does not appear to offer any advantage after primary debulking surgery.

nodes.description: A model of the HIPEC intervention rather than of the disease. Tumour-bearing mice are heated externally across the abdomen to a target of 42 degrees Celsius and given cisplatin, substituting external heating for the intraperitoneal perfusion circuit used clinically, so that hyperthermic chemotherapy can be given without laparotomy and to several animals per procedure. The authors report attenuated tumour growth, delayed ascites and longer survival relative to normothermic cisplatin. Reported in a non-peer-reviewed preprint.

evidence.reference_title: Development of a noninvasive murine model of hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) treatment for ovarian cancer
evidence.snippet: We have developed the first non-invasive animal model by using external abdominal heat with chemotherapy.

nodes.description: Ovarian cancer typically metastasizes by shedding into ascites rather than first through the bloodstream. Tumor cells form multicellular spheroids that survive in suspension and implant across peritoneal surfaces.

animal_models.background: C57BL/6J and NSG mice bearing intraperitoneal syngeneic (ID8-luc, IE9) ovarian tumour cells
animal_models.description: Intraperitoneal tumour cells establish peritoneal disease with ascites, and hyperthermic cisplatin is applied to that compartment as the perturbation. The model manipulates peritoneal dissemination under hyperthermic chemotherapy; it does not claim to reproduce the human transcoelomic mechanism itself.
animal_models.name: Noninvasive external-abdominal-heat HIPEC mouse model

evidence.reference_title: Mesothelial cells interact with tumor cells for the formation of ovarian cancer multicellular spheroids in peritoneal effusions.
evidence.snippet: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) dissemination is primarily mediated by the shedding of tumor cells from the primary site into ascites where they form multicellular spheroids that rapidly lead to peritoneal carcinomatosis.

nodes.description: Ovarian cancer metastases depend on angiogenic support within the peritoneal cavity, and anti-VEGF therapy remains part of maintenance treatment for advanced-stage disease.

evidence.snippet: Most patients with advanced-stage ovarian cancer receive maintenance therapy with bevacizumab (a monoclonal antibody that blocks angiogenesis) and/or poly-adenosine diphosphate ribose polymerase (PARP) inhibitors.
